summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted with left flank pain, fever, and nausea, initially concerning for pyelonephritis. Imaging and urology evaluation showed no active kidney infection or obstruction, with stable bilateral hydronephrosis. Instead, he was found to have cellulitis of the right foot, likely from trauma and recent toenail removal. He developed an allergic reaction to linezolid, which was discontinued, and was successfully treated with clindamycin. His pain improved with management of muscle spasms and infection. Hypertension was managed with restart of amlodipine. He remained afebrile with stable labs, including creatinine around 3.4, and was discharged home in improved condition on a full course of clindamycin, with follow-up planned for blood pressure, mood, and vaccination status.
